ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the upper right terminal is P and the lower one is Q; between P and Q there is a vertical 1Ω resistor, and current i0 is marked on this branch with direction downward. On the left there is a 10V independent voltage source, whose upper end is positive and lower end is negative; on the left there is also a vertical 1Ω resistor connected to its upper and lower nodes. In the middle there is a horizontal 1Ω resistor connecting the upper-left node and P. At the top there is a controlled voltage source, with the left end marked “-” and the right end marked “+”, the voltage is 3i0, connecting the upper-left node and P. At the bottom there is a 1Ω resistor connecting the lower-left node and Q. Then reason: According to the specified labels, let the upper-left node be A, the lower-left node be B, P be node C, and Q be node D. When finding the Thevenin equivalent resistance, short-circuit the independent 10V voltage source, so A and B are combined as the reference ground; the controlled voltage source remains active. Set the port test current source It from Q toward P, so the port current It enters terminal P. Let the voltages of P and Q to ground be VP and VQ, respectively. Since the current i0 on the vertical 1Ω resistor between P-Q is downward, i0 = (VP - VQ)/1. The right end of the controlled voltage source is positive and the left end is grounded, so VP - 0 = 3i0 = 3(VP - VQ). Write KCL at node Q, considering the 1Ω resistor between P-Q, the bottom 1Ω resistor from Q to ground, and the test current source: (VQ - VP) + VQ + It = 0. From VP = 3(VP - VQ), obtain VP = 1.5VQ; substituting into KCL gives 2VQ - VP = -It, namely 0.5VQ = -It. Thus VP - VQ = -It. Therefore Rth = (VP - VQ)/It = -1Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe/label the image nodes: let the left upper node be A, the lower-left node be B, P be node C, and Q be node D. To find Rth, short the independent 10 V source so A and B become ground, while the dependent voltage source remains active. Apply a test current source It from Q to P, so It is the port current entering at P. From the dependent source, write V_P - 0 = 3 i0, with i0 = (V_P - V_Q)/1. Hence V_P = 3(V_P - V_Q). Write KCL at Q using the internal 1 Ω P-Q resistor, the bottom 1 Ω resistor to ground, and the test current source: (V_Q - V_P) + V_Q + It = 0. Solve these equations to obtain V_P - V_Q = -It, so Rth = (V_P - V_Q)/It = -1 Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe/label the visual circuit: take the lower-left node as reference, so the left upper node is fixed at +10 V by the 10 V source. For the open-circuit terminal voltage, no external element is connected across P-Q, but the internal 1 Ω P-Q resistor remains. Use the dependent-source relation V_P - 10 = 3(V_P - V_Q), and KCL at Q through the P-Q 1 Ω and bottom 1 Ω: (V_Q - V_P) + V_Q = 0. Solve to get Voc = V_P - V_Q = -10 V. On the left there is a 10V independent voltage source, whose upper end is positive and lower end is negative; on the left there is also a vertical 1Ω resistor connected to its upper and lower nodes. In the middle there is a horizontal 1Ω resistor connecting the upper-left node and P. At the top there is a controlled voltage source, with the left end marked “-” and the right end marked “+”, the voltage is 3i0, connecting the upper-left node and P. Then reason: According to the specified labels, let the upper-left node be A, the lower-left node be B, P be node C, and Q be node D. When finding the Thevenin equivalent resistance, short-circuit the independent 10V voltage source, so A and B are combined as the reference ground; the controlled voltage source remains active. Set the port test current source It from Q toward P, so the port current It enters terminal P. Let the voltages of P and Q to ground be VP and VQ, respectively. Since the current i0 on the vertical 1Ω resistor between P-Q is downward, i0 = (VP - VQ)/1. The right end of the controlled voltage source is positive and the left end is grounded, so VP - 0 = 3i0 = 3(VP - VQ). Write KCL at node Q, considering the 1Ω resistor between P-Q, the bottom 1Ω resistor from Q to ground, and the test current source: (VQ - VP) + VQ + It = 0. From VP = 3(VP - VQ), obtain VP = 1.5VQ; substituting into KCL gives 2VQ - VP = -It, namely 0.5VQ = -It. Thus VP - VQ = -It. Therefore Rth = (VP - VQ)/It = -1Ω.
